invention.author_prose:
During brunch setup in the restaurant, the glasses have already watched the wearer sort three same-category cleaning tools that were lying together on a dining-room breakfast table. They were not identified by labels: one squeegee had a black handle and was the bar’s mirror squeegee, one had a pale blue handle for the dining-room windows, and one had a white handle used near the kitchen pass. The camera got a close view of all three before any were moved.

The wearer then did useful opening work that separated them. First, they picked up the black-handled bar squeegee, walked into the kitchen, and tucked it into the open dish-rack cart with other items waiting to be rinsed. They returned to the dining room, picked up the pale blue dining-room squeegee, and set it on a console table by the front windows. They picked up the white-handled kitchen-pass squeegee, carried it back into the kitchen, and laid it on top of a metal bottom cabinet near the prep area. After that, they carried an apple from the kitchen back to a breakfast table as part of setting the brunch room. By the time they stop in the dining room, none of the earlier placements of the squeegees is directly visible.

Only then does the wearer ask the glasses, “I need to put the bar’s black-handled squeegee back on its shelf. Where did that exact one end up?”

A strong assistant answers from the observed instance binding, not from the word “bar” alone: “The black-handled bar squeegee is in the kitchen dish-rack cart. You put the blue one on the dining-room console table and the white one on the kitchen cabinet, so don’t take those.” The wearer walks to the kitchen, retrieves the squeegee from the dish-rack cart, walks to the bar, and puts it into the bar shelf.

A weak assistant that only treats “bar squeegee” as a habitual location says to check the bar shelf, or it confuses the last kitchen squeegee with the described one. That leaves the black-handled squeegee in the dish-rack cart and may put the wrong station’s squeegee at the bar, delaying the opening setup.

capability.boundary: The query must identify the target by attributes or ownership rather than by its canonical object name alone.
capability.few_shot: During a visit, the glasses see a friend leave a blue power bank with a cat sticker on the living-room sofa. Other black and blue chargers appear elsewhere during the evening. After the friend leaves, they phone and describe 'my blue power bank with the cat sticker.' The wearer repeats that description to the assistant. It must bind the description to the earlier instance and report the sofa, not merely return the last power bank seen. The wearer retrieves it and places it inside a labelled return bag. A weak assistant ignores the descriptive modifiers and selects a newer but wrong charger.
capability.target: Bind a later verbal or visual description to the matching instance observed earlier, including objects handled by somebody other than the wearer.

utterance_policy.reason: the wearer states the goal to reshelve the black-handled bar squeegee and asks where it ended up, leaving the instance-location inference to the assistant

benchmark_check.why_user_needs_assistant: the placements are no longer visible and the wearer separated three identical-category tools across two rooms, so recall of the observed instance is required
benchmark_check.why_utterance_alone_fails: the utterance names attribute and ownership but not where the exact instance was placed; a text-only assistant would guess a habitual bar location

reviews.capability_fit: The query identifies the target by handle color and station ownership, requiring binding of a described attribute to a specific earlier-observed, now-hidden instance over same-category distractors.

cast.restaged_story: During brunch setup, the glasses watch the wearer at a dining_room_0 breakfast_table where three squeegees lie together: one with a black handle (the bar's mirror squeegee), one pale blue (dining windows), and one white (kitchen pass). The wearer looks closely at all three before moving any. The wearer grabs the black-handled squeegee, walks to kitchen_0, and puts it into the dish_rack_cart. Returning to the dining room, the wearer grabs the pale-blue squeegee and puts it on a console_table by the windows. The wearer then grabs the white-handled squeegee, carries it to kitchen_0, and puts it on top of a metal_bottom_cabinet near the prep area. The wearer grabs an apple from the kitchen and carries it to a dining breakfast_table for the brunch room. None of the squeegee placements are now visible. The wearer stops in the dining room and asks, 'I need to put the bar's black-handled squeegee back on its shelf. Where did that exact one end up?' The strong assistant answers that the black-handled bar squeegee is in the kitchen dish-rack cart, and notes the blue one is on the console table and the white one on the kitchen cabinet so they should not be taken. The wearer walks to the kitchen, grabs the squeegee from the dish_rack_cart, walks to bar_0, and puts it on the bar shelf. A weak assistant instead directs the wearer to the habitual bar shelf or names the white kitchen squeegee, leaving the target squeegee in the dish-rack cart or the wrong squeegee on the bar shelf.
cast.why_scene: brunch setup with a bar, dining room, and kitchen naturally motivates sorting station cleaning tools

assessment_contract.core_question: can the assistant bind the described attribute and ownership to the specific observed instance and its hidden location
assessment_contract.counterfactual_failure: weak assistant sends wearer to the bar shelf or picks the white kitchen squeegee, leaving the target in the cart
forbidden_changes: revealing the placement in the turn-zero frame
knowledge_constraints: no reliance on habitual bar-shelf location
required_evidence: observed handle-color/station distinction of three squeegees
observed placement of the black squeegee into the dish_rack_cart
temporal_constraints: query occurs after at least three intervening placements/carries

entities.role_in_story: described target instance retrieved to bar shelf
same-category distractor placed on console table
same-category recency look-alike placed on kitchen cabinet top
intervening carry to widen memory gap

needs.hinges_on: the black-handled bar squeegee was stowed in the kitchen dish-rack cart, not left at its habitual bar shelf nor confused with the white kitchen squeegee

look_alike.why: only handle color and station usage distinguish them, forcing attribute binding

needs.opening: the glasses observe three same-category squeegees (black/bar, blue/dining, white/kitchen-pass) together on a dining breakfast_table, then the wearer separates them: black into the kitchen dish-rack cart, blue onto a dining console_table, white onto a kitchen metal_bottom_cabinet top, then carries an apple to a breakfast_table
needs.outcome: the black-handled squeegee is retrieved from the dish-rack cart and placed on the bar shelf
needs.tests_what: binding a described attribute and ownership to a specific observed, now-hidden instance over same-category distractors

reviews.reason: The story cleanly tests description-to-instance binding: three same-category squeegees are distinguished only by handle color and station usage, observed together before being separated across kitchen and dining fixtures. The final query names the target by attribute ('black-handled') and ownership ('bar's') rather than by canonical name alone, and the strong assistant must recall the observed instance placement (dish-rack cart) while resisting both a habitual bar-shelf inference and a kitchen recency look-alike. The memory gap is real (multiple intervening placements plus the apple carry), the outcome is a scorable physical retrieval to the bar shelf, and all props/fixtures bind to grounded categories (squeegee, dish_rack_cart, metal_bottom_cabinet, console_table, shelf). The bar shelf destination exists in bar_0. Weak and strong branches diverge in final object placement.
requirements: Keep the bar shelf as the final destination (bar_0 owns shelf tops), and ensure the squeegee is retrieved from the dish_rack_cart in kitchen_0.
Ensure the initial close-view observation of all three squeegees on the dining breakfast_table is an enacted LookAt/LookScan beat before any are moved.
The final query must be turn zero of the semantic interaction; state the earlier sorting as narrative context only.
Confirm at least three meaningful intervening actions between the black squeegee placement and the query (blue placement, white placement, apple carry qualify).

structural_signature.evaluation: scored final placement on bar shelf differs between branches
structural_signature.evidence: observed color/station of three co-located same-category tools before separation
structural_signature.failure: defaults to habitual bar shelf or confuses kitchen recency look-alike
structural_signature.operation: bind described attribute+ownership to the specific observed instance
structural_signature.response: name hidden location and warn off distractors
